scope: Manual review of the ten trial inferred mechanics left pending after conservative textual recommendations.

decisions.rationale: Source text describes moving swirls that apply the curse on contact and explode onto nearby players, directly supporting an area hazard whose safe handling depends on player separation/positioning.
Source text describes an attack aimed at the taunted target and does not establish an area attack; the current inferred mechanic_type=area_attack is not source-supported.
Source text explicitly describes a Fire Behemoth entering from the Oblivion portal at fixed health thresholds, supporting the add-spawn/summon mechanic classification.

The source supports an area attack and lingering hazard, but it says the attack can be performed near or farther from the target; it does not establish requires_positioning=true, so the current inferred row is not lossless.

Source text explicitly names two targets, prioritizes farthest players, requires walking into pools to cleanse, and states that pools remain poisonous for a duration, supporting movement, positioning, cleanse, target-count, and persistence fields.

Source text explicitly describes Havocrel Annihilators entering at health thresholds and states that boss/add proximity causes enrage and that the last add can be held away, supporting summon and positioning fields.

Source text says Rapid Deluge targets five players normally but six on hard mode; the current unscoped target_count=5 loses a documented difficulty-specific value and is not safe to canonicalize as-is.
Source text describes a spell flung at targets and does not establish an area attack; the current inferred mechanic_type=area_attack is unsupported.

The source supports cleansing and careful synergy placement, but the row conflates magical damage-over-time with a later physical glob explosion and marks failure_is_fatal=true without explicit source support; the current inferred row is not lossless.

Source text requires players to distinguish the real Xalvakka by standing very close, and the phase description documents limited safe ground around copies, directly supporting the positioning requirement.
